title: Repossession and Collateral Recovery Right-to-Cure Notices and Notice Status Rules
content:
Legal department note on the right-to-cure notice and on the case statuses in which Repossession and Collateral Recovery notices may be mailed.

**Notice statuses.** Notices are mailed only on a case in pre-repossession review, recovered or sold status: right-to-cure notices in pre-repossession review, the notice of intent to sell and the personal property notice in recovered, and the post-sale explanation in sold.

| Notice | Case status in which it is mailed |
|---|---|
| Right-to-cure notice | pre-repossession review |
| Notice of intent to sell | recovered |
| Personal property notice | recovered |
| Post-sale explanation | sold |

The status test reads the case status on record at the time of mailing; a case in assigned status, or in reinstated, redeemed or recalled status, carries none of these notices.

**The right-to-cure notice.** When the contract's state is listed in the right-to-cure schedule, a right-to-cure notice must be mailed by first-class mail before the case can be assigned, no earlier than when the contract is 10 days past due (the class minimum for a cure notice); its cure deadline is the mailing date plus the state's cure days, and the amount it states is the installments past due on the mailing date plus the contract's fees due.

No new cure notice is needed when a cure notice on an earlier case of the same contract was cured within the last 12 months (the class repeat window), that is when at least one such cured notice is counted on the contract; a contract state not listed in the schedule needs no cure notice.

A right-to-cure notice is cured only when the stated amount is paid on the contract by the cure deadline, in which case the case is recalled with recall reason account brought current.

## Worked illustration (hypothetical contract)

A KS contract (20 cure days) whose notice is mailed on 3 June states a cure deadline of 23 June. If the stated amount is paid on the contract on 23 June, the notice is cured; a payment of the stated amount on 24 June does not cure it.
